direction: Hierarchical human-alignment of pretrained vision foundation models: distilling THINGS-triplet-shaped human-similarity structure (via a SigLIP-So400m teacher) into DINOv2 ViT-B and testing multi-level Spearman gain, behavioural/uncertainty match, downstream utility, and OOD robustness.

behaviors.statement: A THINGS-triplet-fit SigLIP-So400m teacher, distilled into DINOv2 ViT-B via a dedicated alignment loss, injects hierarchical human-similarity structure into the student that improves human-triplet Spearman + reproduces human behaviour/uncertainty, while trading off fine-grained one-shot utility (this trade-off attenuates but does not disappear under LoRA-scope adaptation).
behaviors.behavior_conclusion: The alignment-injection phenomenon holds strongly on its target metrics: a THINGS-fit SigLIP-So400m teacher beats unaligned SigLIP + chance by +13pp on held-out THINGS triplets, and distilling it into DINOv2 ViT-B yields a +0.366 aggregate Spearman gain vs the unaligned student (77% of the gain is human-alignment-specific vs a matched-cost non-aligned control, ruling out generic KD-as-label-smoothing). The aligned student also reproduces human behaviour + uncertainty + RSA on all three tested predicates. However, the alignment recipe also produces a general-ability degradation: aligned DINOv2 loses on fine-grained one-shot classification (mean Δ = −28pp under full α=1.0 KD, attenuated to −24pp under LoRA r=16), and OOD gains concentrate specifically on BREEDS-style subpopulation-shift splits (BREEDS super13/26 win) rather than uniformly across all held-out splits. Adaptation scope, not loss weight, is the utility bottleneck (LoRA scope > full-backbone α↓).

mechanisms.family: Representation and Parameter Analysis / Parameter-Space Task Vectors
mechanisms.headline: The alignment finetune's task vector τ_aligned = θ_M3 − θ_pretrained produces a large + specific Spearman gain (+0.366 aggregate, robust to a smaller-student swap at robustness=1.00; 77% of the gain is human-alignment-specific vs a matched-cost non-human-aligned control τ_control = θ_M5 − θ_pretrained). Behavioural + uncertainty + RSA match human data on all three predicates. But apply_to(base, α=1.0) with full-backbone scope damages fine-grained downstream utility (−28pp mean 1-shot), and OOD gains concentrate specifically on BREEDS-style subpopulation-shift splits. LoRA scope (r=16, α=1.0) is the strictly best attainable regime for utility preservation — the trade-off attenuates (−24pp) and BREEDS super13 gain grows (+0.201 → +0.248) — but does not disappear. α↓ from 1.0 to 0.1 does NOT help (adaptation scope, not loss weight, is the utility bottleneck).

claims.statement: A THINGS-fit SigLIP-So400m teacher head strictly beats unaligned SigLIP-So400m and 1/3 chance on held-out THINGS odd-one-out triplets.
claims.method: Triplet-KL fit of a small alignment head on frozen SigLIP-So400m features; held-out triplet-choice accuracy vs unaligned + chance with bootstrap CI95.
claims.conclusion: Teacher head reaches 0.590 [0.582, 0.598] triplet accuracy vs unaligned SigLIP 0.460 [0.452, 0.467] and chance 0.333, non-overlapping CI95 on both comparisons — audit passed, swap-test deferred (max_verify_claims cap).

claims.statement: The THINGS-fit teacher's triplet-choice signal on ImageNet-synthesised triplets is monotonically level-organised across coarse / mid / fine (each level above chance; ordering pre-declared).
claims.method: Forward-only per-triplet choice-agreement rate at each hierarchy level on 3,000 ImageNet-WordNet triplets (1,000 per level).
claims.conclusion: All three levels beat chance (coarse=0.750, mid=0.747, fine=0.817), but ordering is fine > coarse ≈ mid — not strictly monotonic (likely SigLIP training-signal bias toward basic-level distinctions); audit passed, swap-test deferred (max_verify_claims cap).

claims.statement: Alignment finetune of DINOv2 ViT-B against the THINGS-fit teacher increases aggregate Spearman correlation with human THINGS-triplet similarity by Δρ ≥ 0.05 vs the unaligned baseline.
claims.method: M3 full-backbone KD finetune (triplet_kl loss, α=1.0, lr=5e-5) against the M1 teacher on a 40k ImageNet-val subset; held-out THINGS Spearman vs M4 with paired-bootstrap α=0.05.
claims.conclusion: Robust across a model swap (DINOv2 ViT-B → ViT-S variant also produced Δρ=+0.324 vs main +0.366; robustness=1.00): aligned finetune yields a +0.366 aggregate Spearman gain, 7× the required +0.05 threshold, with non-overlapping CI95.

claims.statement: The aggregate Spearman gain in C2a holds separately at each of the coarse / mid / fine abstraction levels.
claims.method: Per-level Spearman on THINGS held-out, aligned − unaligned; predicted-direction gain required at each of coarse / mid / fine.
claims.conclusion: Coarse (Δρ=+0.526) + mid (Δρ=+0.427) established with non-overlapping CI95; fine level yielded 0 Spearman-usable pairs under the current stratification (construction artifact, not under-power) — audit WARN, swap-test deferred (max_verify_claims cap).

claims.statement: The C2a Spearman gain is specifically attributable to human-similarity alignment (aligned student strictly beats a matched non-human-aligned soft-label control), not to generic KD label smoothing.
claims.method: M5 matched-schedule finetune with unaligned SigLIP-So400m soft labels (no THINGS fit); paired-bootstrap Spearman comparison against M3 on THINGS held-out.
claims.conclusion: 77% of the aligned gain is human-alignment-specific (aligned Δ = 4.3× control Δ; +0.281 of +0.366 aggregate Spearman) — rules out generic KD-as-label-smoothing as the primary driver; audit passed, swap-test deferred (max_verify_claims cap).

claims.statement: The aligned DINOv2 ViT-B more accurately reproduces human behaviour AND per-triplet uncertainty than the unaligned baseline, conjunctively across choice-agreement, uncertainty-KL / uncertainty-Spearman, and RSA.
claims.method: M6 forward-only behavioural + uncertainty comparison on 36,187 THINGS testset2 vs testset2_repeat two-worker triplets; three predicates (choice, uncertainty, RSA) with paired-bootstrap α=0.05.
claims.conclusion: All 3 predicates met in the predicted direction (choice_acc 0.586 vs 0.434; uncertainty_spearman 0.054 vs 0.017 — weak but correct direction; RSA_spearman 0.555 vs 0.189); audit passed, swap-test deferred (max_verify_claims cap).

claims.statement: The aligned DINOv2 ViT-B is non-inferior to the unaligned baseline on downstream one-shot classification (4-of-10 stratified subset).
claims.method: M7 per-dataset 1-shot cosine/linear-probe top-1 with paired-bootstrap non-inferiority test on 4 substitute datasets (DTD / Fashion-MNIST / imagenet_val_top100 / imagenet_val_top20).
claims.conclusion: Falsified as originally stated (mean Δ = −0.284 under α=1.0 full-backbone KD; iter 1 α↓ falsified, iter 2 LoRA attenuated to −0.239); rewritten as C4a_v2 — 'documented one-shot fine-grained classification trade-off, LoRA best-regime' — retracts the preserved/improved fine-grained utility framing.

claims.statement: The aligned DINOv2 ViT-B strictly improves OOD robustness over the unaligned baseline on every held-out split (BREEDS panel + ImageNet-A).
claims.method: M8 feature-extraction + protocol-standard top-1 per split on 5 substitute OOD splits (BREEDS super13/26 + imagenet_val_20_easy/hard + fashion_mnist_ood).
claims.conclusion: Falsified as originally stated (2/5 splits win under every regime — both true subpopulation-shift OOD: BREEDS super13 Δ=+0.201 → +0.248 under LoRA best-regime, super26 Δ=+0.115 → +0.080); rewritten as C4b_v2 — 'selective OOD-robustness gains on BREEDS-style subpopulation-shift only, not universal'.

claims.statement: Under LoRA-scope alignment (r=16, α=1.0), the aligned DINOv2 ViT-B exhibits a documented one-shot fine-grained classification trade-off vs the unaligned baseline; the original preserved/improved fine-grained utility claim is retracted.
claims.method: M7 1-shot cosine/linear-probe top-1 with paired-bootstrap across three adaptation regimes {full α=1.0, full α=0.1, LoRA α=1.0}; narrowing anchors the claim to the honestly-supported best regime.
claims.conclusion: LoRA best-regime mean Δ = −0.239 (attenuated from full α=1.0's −0.284; α↓ falsified at Δ=−0.294); adaptation scope, not loss weight, is the utility bottleneck; audit passed (rewrite), swap-test deferred (max_verify_claims cap).

claims.statement: Under LoRA-scope alignment (r=16, α=1.0), the aligned DINOv2 ViT-B shows selective OOD-robustness gains concentrated on BREEDS-style subpopulation-shift splits; the universal-per-split claim is retracted.
claims.method: M8 protocol-standard top-1 per split across three adaptation regimes; narrowing ties the supported gain to BREEDS-style subpopulation-shift.
claims.conclusion: LoRA best-regime BREEDS super13 Δ=+0.248 (up from +0.201 full-backbone), super26 Δ=+0.080; imagenet_val_20_easy/hard and fashion_mnist_ood all negative; alignment reshapes representation toward taxonomy-compatible subpopulation-shift structure, not universal OOD robustness; audit passed (rewrite), swap-test deferred (max_verify_claims cap).
